title: 黑客把冰柜变成了烤箱

segments.zh: On the night of October 11, freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets
segments.en: 10月11日夜里，法国几百家超市的冰柜，

segments.zh: were remotely heated to 50 degrees Celsius.
segments.en: 被黑客远程加热到了50度。

segments.zh: That's 122 Fahrenheit.
The ice cream did not survive.
Today's question: a freezer makes cold, right?
segments.en: 今天的问题：冰柜明明是造冷的，

segments.zh: So how do you turn it into an oven?
Meet Scoop.
Scoop is an ice cream cone, and Scoop is nervous today.
segments.en: 小勺是一个冰淇淋，今天它很紧张。

segments.zh: According to reports, at least 300 Intermarché and Netto stores
segments.en: 据报道，光是英特马歇和奈拓，

segments.zh: were hit.
Carrefour said 80 more, plus several other chains.
segments.en: 家乐福说80家，还有好几家连锁也中招。

segments.zh: Some equipment even started to catch fire.
segments.en: 有的设备甚至开始冒火。

segments.zh: One boss estimated the damage:
tens of millions of euros, in a single day.
First, a surprise: a fridge doesn't make cold at all.
segments.en: 先说一个反常识：冰箱根本不会“造冷”。

segments.zh: It moves heat.
Like bailing a boat with a sponge:
segments.en: 就像用海绵从船里舀水：

segments.zh: soak it up inside, squeeze it out outside.
segments.en: 在里面吸饱，到外面拧干。

segments.zh: The refrigerant evaporates inside and soaks up heat.
segments.en: 冷媒在柜子里蒸发，吸走热量，

segments.zh: The compressor squeezes it, and the coils outside dump that heat.
segments.en: 压缩机一挤，在外面的管子上把热放掉。

segments.zh: That's why the back of a fridge feels warm.
segments.en: 所以冰箱背后总是热乎乎的。

segments.zh: That's your food's heat.
Twist one: every freezer already has a heater
built right in.
segments.en: 本来就装着一个加热器。

segments.zh: Freezers grow frost, and the thicker the frost,
segments.en: 因为冷柜会结霜，霜越厚，

segments.zh: the worse they move heat.
So every so often a heater melts the ice away.
segments.en: 所以它定时开一会儿加热，把霜化掉，

segments.zh: It's called defrost.
French media reported that's exactly what the attackers did:
segments.en: 据法国媒体报道，黑客做的就是：

segments.zh: forced defrost, and kept it on.
All of this runs on a small connected controller,
segments.en: 控制这一切的，是一个联网的小盒子，

segments.zh: so repair companies can manage it remotely.
segments.en: 好让维修公司远程管理。

segments.zh: Most of the hit units were old models
the maker had stopped updating years ago.
segments.en: 厂家早就不再给它们更新。

segments.zh: Twist two: if a freezer simply loses power,
it's usually fine.
The US Department of Agriculture says a full freezer, door closed,
segments.en: 美国农业部说，装满的冰柜关着门，

segments.zh: holds for about 48 hours.
Because melting ice swallows a lot of heat:
segments.en: 因为冰要化，得先吃进一大口热：

segments.zh: 334 joules for every gram.
Ice is a heat sponge.
It buys your food time.
But a heater cooks it from the inside.
segments.en: 可加热器是从里面往上烤。

segments.zh: No sponge can keep up with that.
50 degrees is almost as hot
as Death Valley on its hottest days.
Twist three: even if the food freezes again,
segments.en: 反转三：就算东西又冻回去了，

segments.zh: it all goes in the trash.
Between 4 and 60 degrees is the danger zone.
Bacteria can double in about 20 minutes.
segments.en: 细菌大约20分钟就能翻一倍。

segments.zh: One becomes two, two becomes four.
segments.en: 一个变两个，两个变四个，

segments.zh: In two hours, that's six doublings.
Freezing only puts bacteria to sleep.
It doesn't kill them.
So the rule is: two hours in the danger zone,
segments.en: 所以规矩是：在危险区待过两小时，

segments.zh: and out it goes.
That's why overnight,
segments.en: 这就是为什么一夜之间，

segments.zh: whole shelves went empty.
One security analyst says stores in Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium
segments.en: 据一位安全分析师说，西班牙、葡萄牙、波兰、德国、比利时

segments.zh: were affected too.
Friendly fine print: so far, officials haven't said who did it,
segments.en: 友情提示：到目前为止，是谁干的、

segments.zh: or how they got in.
segments.en: 怎么进去的，官方都还没说。

segments.zh: France's cyber agency gave simple advice:
segments.en: 法国网络安全部门的建议很朴素：

segments.zh: unplug those boxes from the internet, or lock the door.
segments.en: 把这些盒子从网上断开，或者把门锁好。

segments.zh: Anything you can control from far away,
someone else might, too.
So, your smart gadgets at home?
Keep them updated.
Scoop is fine. Scoop lives in a home freezer.
segments.en: 小勺没事，它在家里的冰箱里。

segments.zh: Yours isn't online... is it?
